summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of end-stage renal disease, polycystic kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, and recurrent bacteremia presented from dialysis with rigors and a temperature of 100°F. She reported persistent fatigue, malaise, and chronic back pain since completing a course of cefazolin for Klebsiella bacteremia 10 days prior. She had recent dental work and took an unknown prophylactic antibiotic. Initial labs showed stable leukocyte count, elevated calcium at 11.0 mg/dL, and subtherapeutic INR of 1.3. A chest X-ray revealed small bilateral pleural effusions and mild pulmonary congestion without pneumonia. She was started on empiric vancomycin and cefepime. Blood cultures and CMV viral load were negative. Given lack of ongoing symptoms, absence of infection markers, and no growth in cultures, antibiotics were discontinued. Her hypercalcemia was managed with continuation of cinacalcet and sevelamer, holding vitamin D, and using a low-calcium dialysis bath. Warfarin was adjusted to improve INR, which rose to 1.6. She remained clinically stable, afebrile, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up and monitoring of pending SPEP and calcium levels.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Personal history of allergy to penicillin
Personal history of allergy to sulfonamides
